A1.justification: Both readable 10-page PDFs describe SVBench and support comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures. All supplied pages were inspected. Neither PDF contains a separate appendix, despite Section 3.1 mentioning one; comparison covers all material actually supplied.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of eight video generators on 15 tasks, human assessment of generated prompts, difficulty experiments, and comparisons between automated and human judgments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Tables 2–4 and Figures 3–4.

M1.justification: The four-agent pipeline, prompt critique and revision procedure, cue manipulation, five binary evaluation dimensions, and score aggregation remain unchanged. The added long-tail discussion does not specify a procedural change.

E1.justification: Table 1 retains the same 30 seed paradigms and 15 tasks selected for short-video evaluation. The replacement illustration in Figure 1 does not establish changed experimental coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same eight generators, including Wan2.2. Table 4 retains the same four closed-source models, and Table 3 compares the same pipeline stages. The newly cited methods are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Both versions retain the 5–10-second task design, Gemini 2.5 Pro judge, five binary scoring dimensions, three difficulty levels, and human-validation sample of 20 videos per model, totaling 160 clips.

E4.justification: The pipeline-stage validation, cue-difficulty analysis, automated-versus-human comparison, and two qualitative evaluation cases are unchanged (Tables 3–4 and Figures 3–4). No analysis accompanies the new long-tail discussion.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same pass-rate summaries without seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No statistical reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 have identical numerical entries, including overall scores of 79.6% for Sora2pro and 72.4% for Veo-3.1. The Figure 3 plots and Figure 4 cases are also unchanged. Figure 1's replacement illustration reports no new scored result.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 retains the same binary dimension definitions and arithmetic-mean score. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced; the long-tail passage is informal motivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about the first social-reasoning video benchmark, its training-free agent pipeline, and current generators' social-reasoning limitations.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly describes social behavior as long-tailed, identifies rare interactions as difficult to model, and links curiosity-driven cooperation to selecting evaluation dimensions. Interpretations of model performance, cue sensitivity, and human–judge differences remain unchanged.

D1.justification: No implementation settings, hyperparameters, hardware information, or reproducibility resources are added or revised. The project URL is unchanged; removing its 'Project Page' label does not alter access information.

R1.justification: v2 adds three sources concerning cryptocurrency early warning, GRU-CNN-GA feature stability, and curiosity-driven long-tailed multi-label learning ([21], [22], [55]). Brief connections appear in Sections 1, 2.1, and 3.1, without changing the central novelty positioning. Morpheus was already referenced in v1.

P1.justification: Three short contextual passages are inserted, the malformed Morpheus citation is repaired, and the project-link label is removed. The remaining prose and section order are substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1(a) replaces the boy/tool-selection frames and prompt with the crying-girl/ice-cream scenario described in the introduction. Existing displays undergo limited relocation: Table 2 moves from page 6 to 7, Figure 3 from page 7 to 8, and Figure 4 changes columns.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects v1's Figure 1–introduction mismatch and repairs the malformed Morpheus citation, providing modest gains in clarity and consistency. The added cross-domain passages are loosely connected and partly repetitive, limiting the benefit. The method, experimental evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
